chunks: And it was narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from al-Bāqir Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Regarding testimony upon the testimony of a man while he is present in the town,

He said: "Yes, even if he is behind a column. That is permissible if he is unable to present it himself due to an excuse that prevents him from attending and presenting it; then there is no harm in establishing testimony upon his testimony."

key_terms.إِقَامَةِ الشَّهَادَةِ: the presentation or establishment of testimony
key_terms.الشَّهَادَةِ: legal testimony or witness statement in a judicial context
key_terms.بِالْحَضْرَةِ: being present nearby or within reach
key_terms.سَارِيَةٍ: a column or pillar, indicating physical presence but lack of direct appearance
key_terms.شَهَادَةِ الرَّجُلِ: the testimony of the original male witness
key_terms.لِعِلَّةٍ: due to an excuse, impediment, or valid disabling cause
key_terms.يَحْضُرَ: to attend in person before the authority

ai.seo_question: Is testimony upon another person's testimony valid if the original witness is present in the same town but unable to appear?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on testimony based on another person's testimony. Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام permits it when the original witness cannot personally appear and present the testimony due to a valid excuse, even if he is physically in the town.
